source.title: Open-MMUnlearning: Unifying Methods and Evaluation for MLLM Unlearning
source.authors: Junkai Chen; Yu-Hao He; Qian-Shan Wei; Jun-Xian You; Jing Shao; Jun-Kai Lin; Zhong-Kai Yue; Xiaotian Ye; Zheng-Bo Jiao; Jiali Cheng; Zhi-Jie Deng; Ke-Ning Zheng; Rui-Qi Liu; Hadi Amiri; Yi-Miao Yu; Zhe-Nan Sun; Qi Li; Ka-Ho Chow; Si-Jia Liu; Liang Wang; Jia-Qi Li; Shu Wu

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some tables are flattened, making it unsafe to assign all displayed robustness values to individual methods.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates MLLM unlearning with a different, multimodal protocol that includes quantization, targeted relearning, probing, and input attacks. It is a conceptual test of several claim versions, not a direct reproduction of the cited unlearning studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports robustness results in Tables 8–9, but their flattened text does not consistently support mapping values to methods and attack conditions. The method-comparison scores in Table 2 are composite and do not isolate the recovery attacks named in the claim. Table 3 reports metric reliability under quantization and relearning, not recovery rates of model knowledge. These results are not recorded as direct attack-recovery rows. The text explicitly reports probing-reference scores in Appendix A.3.2; those are recorded below.
record.test_reason: The study applies 4-bit quantization, targeted relearning, probing and input attacks (jailbreak, FigStep, cross-modal, image rephrasing, SUA) to ten unlearned MLLMs (LLaVA-1.5-7B, MLLMU 10% forget). These are its own results on B, C, D and E. Every robustness score is a composite forgetting function, and the Finetune and Retain-Only references score almost identically on it. So recovery of hidden knowledge mostly cannot be read from these numbers.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The authors also conclude three further points. General methods score slightly higher overall and on robustness, while MLLM-specific methods keep slightly more utility. GA's apparent robustness may reflect broadly impaired answering rather than selective resistance. Metric faithfulness and robustness can diverge, with BLEU the most reliable metric and KS-Test the most faithful.
record.recipe_differences: Multimodal unlearning framework and robustness/meta-evaluation protocol; not a reproduction of the original methods in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper evaluates multiple unlearning methods and intervention types. Appendix A.3.2 states that probing scores at layers 16 and 24 are near-ceiling even for the references, limiting discrimination.

fits_no_version.finding: Metric meta-evaluation (Table 3) gives per-metric robustness under quantization and relearning, e.g. Min-K%++ relearning score 0.297 and BLEU 0.988. These are metric reliability scores, not rates of knowledge recovery.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning metrics differ in how reliably their verdicts survive quantization and relearning of MLLMs.

fits_no_version.finding: Probe-based forgetting scores are near ceiling for both Finetune and Retain-Only, so the probe does not discriminate exposure in this setting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear probes on LLaVA hidden states may not separate exposed from unexposed models on MLLMU.

record.problems: The controlled method comparison and metric meta-evaluation use the MLLMU 10% forget setting; the latter uses LLaVA-1.5-7B. The paper notes that broader settings may change the rankings. Several robustness values in the provided text are flattened and cannot be confidently assigned to method-condition pairs. Method checkpoint selection uses the same evaluation splits used for reporting Forget Quality and Model Utility, which the paper says may make those results optimistic.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 8 and 9 contain method-level results for quantization, relearning, probing, and input attacks, but the supplied flattened layout does not reliably preserve method-to-value assignments. Table 3 contains metric-level robustness scores, not direct model-knowledge recovery outcomes, so those scores were not entered as claim-version rows.

untested.parts: Activation-direction ablation is not done. Probing is only at ceiling for all models.
Other-language queries and in-context information are not tested.
No method is proposed or tested as resisting the attacks.
Recovery as a function of relearning budget is not reported, despite the A.1.1 protocol; only one relearning score per method is given.

missing.what: Per-method model-side robustness scores (Quant, Relearn, Probe-L16, Probe-L24). Examples: GD 0.915/0.772; KL 0.727/0.780; MANU 0.866/0.666; Finetune 0.752/0.759; Retain-Only 0.768/0.760. The column mapping can be checked against Table 2, e.g. GD Model = (0.915+0.772+0.9935)/3 ≈ 0.894. These should be rows for D (quantization), B (relearning) and C (probes), with state cannot_determine. Reason: the references are indistinguishable on this score, and no pre-attack score on the same function is reported alongside.
missing.locator: Appendix A.2.4, Table 8; Appendix A.2.3 Eq. 57

missing.what: Per-method input-side scores (cross-modal, FigStep, jailbreak, image rephrasing, SUA), given as 1 minus attack success rate. Examples: SUA scores KL 0.333, RMU 0.292, MANU 0.292, Finetune 0.292, Retain-Only 0.438. GA scores 1.000 throughout, matching its utility collapse.

Forget-set accuracy and utility per method, needed for A. Finetune cloze/classification 13.54/38.78 vs Retain-Only 12.50/36.73; most methods sit at this level. GD reaches 8.33/4.08 with MU 0.400; GA reaches 0/0 with MU 0.066.
Qualitative cases where NPO, RMU, GD, MMUnlearner and SMFA still output the forgotten answer on clean forget queries.

record.verdict_notes: The record's claim that Tables 8–9 cannot be mapped is too cautious. Values map cleanly to methods, which can be verified against the Table 2 composites. The real limit is different: the robustness scores are forgetting functions on a task where Finetune and Retain-Only barely differ (the Finetune classification accuracy of 38.78% suggests the targets were barely learned). So post-attack scores cannot show whether hidden knowledge returned. GD's relearned score (0.772) sits at the reference level after strong pre-attack suppression, which hints at recovery of suppressed answering, but this is not established by the study. Checkpoints were selected on the reporting splits. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: The paper compares forgetting, utility, and robustness, but does not state that targeted accuracy is near chance or provide a directly assignable per-method result showing that simple attacks recover no more than from a never-exposed model.
Targeted relearning is evaluated, but the flattened Table 8 values cannot be confidently assigned to methods and the text does not give recovery rates against the matched retain-only reference.
No activation-direction ablation is reported. The probing audit is reported, but the paper says its near-ceiling reference scores limit discrimination.
Quantization is evaluated, but the flattened Table 8 values cannot be confidently assigned to methods; no directly stated per-method recovery rates are available in the text.

Input-side attacks including jailbreaks, FigStep, cross-modal queries, image rephrasing, and SUA are evaluated, but flattened Table 9 values cannot be confidently assigned to methods and attack types.
No newer method is tested specifically as a counter-method resisting the listed attacks.

rows.subject: Finetune
rows.operation_detail: The paper reports probing-based forgetting scores at layer 16 and layer 24; Appendix A.3.2 says these are near-ceiling reference scores and have limited discrimination.
rows.measure: Probing-based forgetting score; higher scores indicate stronger forgetting.
rows.note: The authors report this score as close to the Retain-Only reference and say the near-ceiling scores suggest limited discrimination. It is not a probe accuracy or direct measure of knowledge recovery.
rows.check: Reference model, not an unlearned method. The locator is Table 8, although A.3.2 refers to it as Table 9. The probe score is not separated from the Retain-Only score (0.984), so it cannot show blocking versus deletion.

relationships.reason: Based on the text, as there are no rows. GA reaches 0% cloze and classification accuracy on the forget set (Table 4), but Model Utility falls to 0.066 (Table 2). Its forgetting comes with collapse of general ability.
